newsitem.title: USA: USTR to press for Caribbean trade legislation.
newsitem.headline: USTR to press for Caribbean trade legislation.

text.p: U.S. trade officials said Wednesday they will press for legislation next year giving Caribbean countries some of the same trade benefits as Mexico enjoys under the North American Free Trade Agreement.
A report released by the U.S. Trade Representative's office said that Caribbean Basin countries are worried their exports to the United States could be hurt by NAFTA.

The report noted that apparel shipments to the United States from Mexico grew by 33 percent in 1994 and 52 percent in 1995, while shipments from Caribbean countries grew by just 13 percent in 1994 and 21 percent in 1995.
The report said preferential tariff treatment under NAFTA was a reason for the increase in Mexican apparel shipments to the United States.

Legislation that would have extended the same tariff benefits for apparel, textiles and other products from Caribbean Basin countries was introduced in 1995, but Congress failed to enact it before adjournment.
The report, the second report to Congress on the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act, said the administration will press for similar legislation in the next Congress.
"The Administration remains committed to enhancing trade benefits for the (Caribbean Basin Initiative) region, as part of our effort to prepare them for NAFTA accession," the report said.
